summaries.label: First Reading
summaries.text: Scripture shut everything under sin so that the promise could be given to those who believe. The law guarded us until Christ came; now, baptized into Christ, all are God’s children, one in him, and heirs of Abraham’s promise.

summaries.label: Psalm
summaries.text: The psalm calls on God’s people to sing, to seek the Lord’s face, and to remember his wonders, and it addresses them as the seed of Abraham and the children of Jacob.

summaries.label: Gospel
summaries.text: A woman in the crowd blesses the womb that bore Jesus. He answers that those who hear the word of God and keep it are blessed.

unity: The psalm’s seed of Abraham and Paul’s heirs of the promise are those who hear God’s word and keep it, as Mary did. Make that concrete today: read one Gospel passage slowly and do the one thing it asks.
lead_in: Luke 11:27–28 blesses the womb that bore Christ; Newman sees in that blessing the oldest promise, to Eve, at last fulfilled.

excerpt.text: In her was now to be fulfilled that promise which the world had been looking out for during thousands of years. The Seed of the woman, announced to guilty Eve, after long delay, was at length appearing upon earth, and was to be born of her. In her the destinies of the world were to be reversed, and the serpent's head bruised.
excerpt.attribution: John Henry Newman, Parochial and Plain Sermons, vol. 2, sermon 12, “The Reverence Due to the Blessed Virgin Mary,” p. 128
